subject: Live trace anomalies after VPC go-live — runbook verification & quick fix plan
messages:
From: David Lin <david.lin@acmecloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Cloud NOC <noc@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Live trace: brief anomalies after go-live — quick sync?

Hi Olga / Marissa,

We completed the VPC cutover at 02:00 UTC and started directed traffic at 08:45 local. Since then we've observed short (~30s) 503 spikes proxied through the new edge. Attached is a pcap snapshot around 08:52 and a small firewall state extract.

High-level observations from our side:
- 503s correlate with SYN/ACK timeouts followed by retransmits
- traceroute from our NOC shows an asymmetric path on one hop (edge-fw-02)

Can your team confirm the planned runbook steps for a next-30m hotfix? We want to minimize customer impact — will hold further traffic changes until we sync.

Thanks,
David
David Lin
Platform Ops, Acme Cloud

Attachments: acme_pcap_snapshot_0915.pcap (pcap), acme_fw_snapshot_0915.json (json)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: David Lin <david.lin@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live trace: brief anomalies after go-live — quick sync?

Thanks David — appreciate the pcap and snapshot. Looping in Rishi and Vivek for immediate triage.

Short plan proposal (30m window):
1) Confirm whether edge-fw-02 ACLs have an unintended deny rule for ephemeral client ports.
2) Hot patch ACL on edge-fw-02 (non-disruptive insert) and validate with live-trace synthetic.
3) If no improvement within 10 minutes of patch, fail traffic back to prior transit for the small customer shard.
4) Post-incident: capture KV warmup/logs and run the runbook validation checklist.

I'm attaching the runbook v2 with the specific ACL checklist highlighted. Rishi/Vivek — please pull the 08:50-08:55 logs and share any immediate red flags.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Principal Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_private_onprem_runbook_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Lin <david.lin@acmecloud.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live trace: brief anomalies after go-live — quick sync?

Olga — quick read of the Acme firewall snapshot shows an ACL sequence mismatch on edge-fw-02: the newly pushed rule set skipped a port-range permit for ephemeral > 32768 on the eastbound ACL. That explains the asymmetric retransmits.

Immediate remediation I recommend:
- Insert temporary allow rule at top of eastbound ACL on edge-fw-02 (non-destructive).
- Run synthetic live-trace from NOC to verify flows (David, please hold on re-routing until we confirm).
- If synthetics pass for 10m, commit fix into next config push and run the runbook's post-apply validation (items 4-7).

I'll prepare the ACL diff and post to SUP-3421.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, David Lin <david.lin@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live trace: brief anomalies after go-live — quick sync?

Adding telemetry context — I pulled the KV cache and edge latencies for the 08:40-09:00 window. Two observations:
- There was a brief KV miss storm when the first customer shards ramped; cache fill started at 08:46 and stabilized by 08:51, coinciding with the 503s.
- Gateway batching at the edge is still on the conservative window (40ms); for this customer shard we can reduce to 25ms temporarily to lower queueing latency while ACL is patched.

Suggested commands we can run during the 30m window (ops team only):
- netctl acl insert edge-fw-02 "allow tcp any any range 32769-65535" --position 1
- gatewayctl set batching --edge edge-az1 --batch-ms 25 --temp 30m

I'll stand by for the ACL diff from Marissa. Also posting a dashboard snapshot to the runbook link.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference

Related: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-3421

Thanks team — we can schedule a 30-minute maintenance window at 16:00 PDT (in 1 hour). We'll keep traffic staged and provide a live synthetic probe during the window.

A couple requests before we start:
- Please circulate the rollback plan in the thread (we want the exact steps and expected timing if we need to fail back to previous transit).
- Confirm who will be the single point of contact for rollback execution.

David

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: David Lin <david.lin@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live trace: brief anomalies after go-live — runbook verification & quick fix plan

Update and closure for today's quick window: we executed the top-insert ACL allow on edge-fw-02 at 16:00 PDT, reduced gateway batching to 25ms for 30m, and ran the synthetic probe sequence. Results:
- Live-trace shows no further 503 spikes during the 30m observation window.
- KV cache ramp completed within ~3 minutes after the batching change; tail latencies improved by ~18%.

Rollback plan (documented and ready if needed):
A) If new 503s recur during maintenance:
  1) Revert gateway batching to 40ms: gatewayctl set batching --edge edge-az1 --batch-ms 40
  2) Re-apply transit routing to previous VIP: routectl set vip acme-shard --target transit-old --time 60s
  3) If traffic still impacted after 60s, open an incident and escalate to infra on-call.
B) If no recurrence (current state):
  1) Commit ACL change into the next config push with the ACL diff (SUP-3421).
  2) Run the runbook post-apply checklist: 5m synthetics, 10m latency burn-in, export logs for audit.

Action items assigned:
- Marissa: post ACL diff to SUP-3421 and schedule commit window (in progress).
- Rishi: capture KV trace and attach to the runbook entry.
- Vivek: run the observability smoke checklist and confirm dashboards show green.

David — thanks for the quick coordination. Please reply here to confirm you consider this closed from Acme's side; we'll keep the runbook entry and artifacts on the shared drive.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Principal Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
